messages:
maria_g: Escalation from acct team — customer reports their private integration to internal-prod.myservice.svc.redwood.internal started failing. They see the name resolve to a public IP (34.120.45.7) and TLS cert mismatch -> 502 from our side. They say this worked before. Repro steps attached in ticket. Can infra investigate?

samir_p: Can you paste the dig/nslookup output and which VPC/account this is in?

maria_g: From their CI runner (inside their VPC):

```
$ dig +short internal-prod.myservice.svc.redwood.internal
34.120.45.7

$ curl -v https://internal-prod.myservice.svc.redwood.internal/health
* SSL: certificate subject name (redwood-public.example.com) does not match target host name 'internal-prod.myservice.svc.redwood.internal'
* HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```

Account: 123456789012 (customer-account-us-east-1). VPC: vpc-0a1b2c3d (10.0.0.0/16). Ticket #INC-9341.

tyler_a: Quick checklist: private hosted zone collision? resolver rules? VPC association mismatch?

samir_p: I'm seeing a private hosted zone named internal-prod.myservice.svc.redwood.internal in *two* accounts: Z1ABC111 (our infra account 555555) and Z9XYZ999 (partner onboarding acct 888888). Both are associated with the same customer VPC (vpc-0a1b2c3d) via cross-account association. That will pick the hosted zone with the lowest hosted zone ID? Route53 private zone behaviour picks the most specific association per VPC — cross-account associations can shadow each other.

maria_g: Is there a way to show which hosted zone is actually answering for the VPC?

samir_p: Yes — from inside the VPC nameserver (AWS default: use resolver IP 169.254.169.253? actually the VPC-provided resolver at the .2 address). Run from an instance in the VPC:

```
$ dig @172.31.0.2 internal-prod.myservice.svc.redwood.internal +short +trace
34.120.45.7
```

But to identify the zone owner we compared records in both hosted zones and found the A record pointing to the public IP only exists in the partner onboarding hosted zone (Z9XYZ999). Our zone (Z1ABC111) has the correct internal private IPs (10.100.5.12).

ops-bot: Ticket INC-9341 created and linked to this thread — priority P1 assigned.

tyler_a: That explains TLS mismatch: customer's client resolves the name to the public IP because the onboarding zone contains an A record for the public IP. How did the partner zone get associated with the customer's VPC? Looks like the onboarding automation ran a cross-account VPC association when they set up shared services.

samir_p: Quick remediation options:
- Remove the association of Z9XYZ999 from the customer's VPC (if onboarding zone shouldn't serve that VPC).
- Delete the conflicting A record from Z9XYZ999 and push a proper internal A into Z1ABC111.
- Create a Route53 Resolver rule in customer account with higher priority to forward queries to the intended nameserver (workaround).

maria_g: Customer prefers minimal change — asked if we can temporarily add a resolver rule to force the right answers. They need a rollback plan.

samir_p: I created a temporary outbound resolver rule in account 123456789012 pointing internal-prod.myservice.svc.redwood.internal -> our internal resolver (10.100.0.2) with priority 10. Tested from their CI runner, results now: 

```
$ dig +short internal-prod.myservice.svc.redwood.internal @172.31.0.2
10.100.5.12
$ curl -sS https://internal-prod.myservice.svc.redwood.internal/health | jq .status
"ok"
```

This fixes the immediate customer impact. We'll coordinate with onboarding to remove the VPC association from Z9XYZ999 or remove the public A-record.

tyler_a: Action items:
- samir_p to request onboarding team to unassociate Z9XYZ999 from vpc-0a1b2c3d and confirm (ETA 2h).
- maria_g to communicate workaround to customer and confirm CI runs green.
- ops-bot to track RCA and add automation guard to prevent cross-account hosted zones from being associated to customer VPCs without an allowlist.

maria_g: Customer verified CI now green. Thanks :thumbsup:. Please keep me posted on removal so they can remove our temporary resolver rule.

samir_p: Onboarding unassociated Z9XYZ999 from the VPC and removed the conflicting A record. I validated answers revert to internal IPs from within VPC.

```
$ dig +short internal-prod.myservice.svc.redwood.internal @172.31.0.2
10.100.5.12
```

tyler_a: I'll file a follow-up ticket for an automation guard and add an alert for cross-account hosted-zone associations.

maria_g: Closing the loop with customer and updating INC-9341 with remediation steps and timeline. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
